Fine-grained access control lets you control who can access certain data within an OpenSearch
Service domain. Compared to generalized access control, ﬁne-grained access control gives each
cluster, index, document, and ﬁeld its own speciﬁed policy for access. Access criteria can be based
on a number of factors, including the role of the person who is requesting access and the action
that they intend to perform on the data. For example, you might give one user access to write to an
index, and another user access only to read the data on the index without making any changes.
Fine-grained access control allows data with diﬀerent access requirements to exist in the same
storage space without running into security or compliance issues.
